manifest.name: dsh-wsl-tool
manifest.description: Extends the working range of DSH into WSL. Files in the distribution can be read, written, edited and searched by DSH directly. Depending on the task, the AI chooses for itself: run a one-off command, or open its own terminal and run several commands there to finish the job. Typing `dsh` in a WSL terminal calls DSH (type `dsh help` there for details), fusing WSL and DSH deeply. Every terminal you open can collaborate visually with the AI.

bundle.text:
# This bundle layer inserts the wsl tool plugin process-wide, so every agent
# preset gets the `wsl`/`wsl-path`/`wsl-env` tools without declaring anything.
#
# Do NOT also add a `tool-wsl` row to a preset. DSH registers tools by name and
# the second registration fails with
# `tool "wsl" is already registered in this scope`. To keep the tools out of a
# composition, override this row by id in a later patch layer (`- id: tool-wsl`
# with `disabled: true`) instead of duplicating it.
#
# This file deliberately changes nothing else: installing a tool plugin must not
# reshape someone's session. Pointing the desktop app's sidebar terminal at WSL is
# offered as an opt-in instead — see `extras/terminal-wsl.patch.yml`.

# The entry name is PATH-RELATIVE on purpose. DSH anchors a relative `name:` to
# the directory of the patch file that declared it (`anchorInsertedPluginNames`),
# so this row always loads this bundle's own `index.js` — whatever the package
# folder happens to be called. A bare package name would instead have to match
# the installed folder name, which couples this file to the npm package name:
# the registry refuses `dsh-wsl` as too similar to `is-wsl`, so the published
# name is `dsh-wsl-tool` while a local `file:` install may sit in
# `node_modules/dsh-wsl`. Keep this relative.

- insert:
    - id: tool-wsl
      name: './index.js'

readme.text:
[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A model-facing **WSL** tool plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It lets an agent run
Linux commands through `wsl.exe` directly — no hand-written `.sh` scripts or `pwsh`
wrappers — and for command execution it essentially matches a native Linux DSH: a
real Linux kernel and bash, exit codes and signals, timeouts, truncation with spill
files, background jobs the built-in job tools read back, stdin, and automatic
Windows/WSL path translation.

It can also work the way you would, in a **shell that keeps its state**: one shell per piece
of work, every command recorded with its exit code, a compact count of that work above the
composer, and — when you name one of your own terminals — the keyboard back in your hands
with one click.

Two limits are worth knowing before you rely on it. A `wsl` call runs below DSH's
sandbox, so a file policy does not confine it (see [Sandboxing](#sandboxing)); and a
project kept on a Windows drive keeps **Windows** filesystem semantics — no POSIX
permissions, case-insensitive names, no file-change notifications — at a fraction
of the speed (see [Notes](#notes)).

The plugin registers ten tools. Each has a switch of its own except `wsl-term`, and
`wsl-doctor` and `wsl-bootstrap` are OFF by default:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wsl` | Run a Linux command and return `stdout`/`stderr` with exit-code, timeout and truncation markers. |
| `wsl-path` | Convert between Windows and WSL paths via `wslpath`. |
| `wsl-env` | Summarize the WSL environment (distros, kernel, cpu, mem, disk). |
| `wsl-doctor` | Compare what a project needs with what the distribution has — including commands that are really Windows binaries. Read-only. **Off by default** (turn it on when diagnosing a project). |
| `wsl-bootstrap` | Install the missing toolchain inside the distribution, from a fixed recipe list, plan first. |
| `wsl-term` | Work in the session's terminal: one shell per piece of work, with a record of each above the composer. |
| `wsl-read` | Read a text file inside the distribution, whole or by line range. Binary and non-UTF-8 files are refused. |
| `wsl-write` | Write a text file inside the distribution, atomically, creating parents. |
| `wsl-edit` | Replace one unique string in a text file inside the distribution. |
| `wsl-grep` | Search file contents inside the distribution with a regular expression, grouped by file with line numbers. |

Runs:

```
wsl.exe [-d <distro>] -e bash -lc "cd <workdir> && <command>"
```

and returns `stdout`/`stderr` with `[exit code: N]` / `[killed by signal: ...]` /
`[timed out after Nms; the command was killed]` / `[output truncated: ...]` markers.

`<distro>` is the caller's `distro` argument, else `DSH_WSL_DISTRO`, else omitted
entirely so `wsl.exe` uses the **system default distribution** — that is what makes
the package portable to a machine that has no `Ubuntu-22.04`.

A script longer than the Windows command-line limit (32767 characters) is fed to
`wsl.exe [-d <distro>] -e bash -ls` on **stdin** instead, so long commands work
without any size ceiling.

Pass `stdin` to write text into the command (the default is `/dev/null`, so an
interactive command gets EOF), and `runInBackground: true` for work that outlives
the call: the command becomes a job in the host's registry, which the model then
reads with the **`job_output`** tool and stops with **`job_kill`** — no extra tool
is involved. Background jobs need `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs` in the preset's
composition; without it the call fails with that instruction instead of silently
running in the foreground.

Converts a path in either direction: `C:\Users\me\a.txt` -> `/mnt/c/Users/me/a.txt`
or `/home/me/a.txt` -> `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-22.04\home\me\a.txt`. Direction is
auto-detected from the path, or forced with `direction: 'win' | 'linux'`.

Returns the distribution list, the probed distro, kernel and architecture, CPU
count, memory and disk usage, and what the machine can actually **do**:

```
distro: Ubuntu-22.04 (system default)
Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64
nproc: 24
Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS · WSL2 · cgroup v2

so an agent can decide what is available before running commands: WSL1 vs WSL2,
whether systemd manages services, the cgroup version (matters for containers),
GPU passthrough, docker (installed / cli-only / daemon version), which drives are
mounted, and how `/etc/wsl.conf` and the Windows-side `.wslconfig` are
configured. Takes an optional `distro`.

Every fact is optional and degrades honestly: a probe that cannot run leaves its
line out, an empty value is stated (`docker: not installed`, `.wslconfig: not
set`), a failed probe is reported in the summary instead of being dropped, and an
unknown distro is an error rather than a partial answer. Note that `wsl --version`
is **localized**, so its labels are passed through as the launcher printed them
rather than parsed by name; the Direct3D/MSRDC/DXCore versions are omitted.

Answers the question a project's own README cannot: **will the tooling this
checkout expects actually work inside this distribution?** It reads the manifests
in the directory (`package.json` and lockfiles, `.nvmrc`, `tsconfig.json`,
`Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `Dockerfile`,
`docker-compose.yml`, `Makefile`, `CMakeLists.txt`) and reports, per need, whether
it resolves on the Linux side:

```
distro: Ubuntu-22.04 (system default)
workspace: /mnt/d/proj (Windows drive mount /mnt/d — builds, installs and git are much slower here; …)
project: package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml

That `WINDOWS` row is the reason the tool exists. WSL appends the Windows `PATH`
to the Linux one, so `npm` resolves on a machine whose distribution has no `node`
at all — measured here as `/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/npm` — and the errors a
model gets from running it against a Linux directory name neither cause. Overall
it is read-only, cheap, and worth running before blaming a failed command on the
command. Takes an optional `workspace` (a Linux directory; default: the configured
directory, else the session workspace) and `distro`.

Installs the missing toolchain **inside the distribution**, from a fixed recipe
list and nothing else: `node` (Node.js LTS into `/usr/local`, checksum-verified,
with corepack), `pnpm`, `python` (python3 + pip + venv), `build`
(build-essential), `tools` (jq, rsync, curl, git, ca-certificates). Dependencies
are added when they are needed: `pnpm` brings `node`, and `node` brings `tools`
when `curl` is missing.

**It is off by default**, and its `dryRun` defaults to `true`, so the first call
prints the plan and changes nothing:

```
dry run — nothing has been installed (distro Ubuntu-22.04)

already present:
  python — python3, pip and venv (apt)

Recipes that are already satisfied are skipped, and the plan includes what apt itself
would do, so you can see the exact changes before anything is installed. Installation
runs as root; a failing step stops the run.

Every other tool here starts a **fresh shell per call**. That is what makes them
safe to run in parallel, and it stays the default. `wsl-term` is the other way
round: **one shell for one piece of work**. It is for the jobs where the shell's own
state is the point — a build worth watching, an interactive program, a directory or
an environment that has to survive between steps.

`wsl-term` works in that terminal:

```
wsl-term({ action: "list" })                                  → which terminals are open
wsl-term({ action: "read" })                                  → the current screen
wsl-term({ action: "run", command: "make sta", subtask: "跑通 sta 流程" })
                                                               → runs it there, returns output and exit code

**Which shell it drives.** Two rules, and the difference is the `subtask` argument:

- **A `run` with a `subtask` is tracked work.** It uses a **private WSL shell this tool opens**:
  one shell per piece of work, every command recorded above the composer, and `subtask-done`
  closes it (or leaves it idle). It is not a sidebar tab and only the tool types into it —
  tracking bookkeeping never touches a terminal you opened.
- **A command without a `subtask` is collaborative.** `run`, `read`, `input` and `interrupt`
  use the newest terminal **you** have open, so you watch the command happen and can read the
  screen afterwards. While the tool works, that terminal is read-only; press 接管输入 to type
  again. The tool **never closes** a terminal you opened.
- **A named `id` always wins**, whichever kind of terminal it is.

If you have no terminal open, an ad-hoc command opens a private shell instead — a normal shell
for that session, but **not a sidebar tab**. The bridge makes the collaborative case possible
on DSH 0.2.1: the host no longer lets a plugin attach to a browser terminal directly, but this
plugin's own browser half runs in the page, where that attachment is allowed, so the host
queues `attach`/`write`/`detach` commands for it over two same-origin routes (no extra port and
no extra service). Older DSH builds (≤0.2.0) are not supported by the terminal tool any more;
the other tools still run there.

Naming a `subtask` on `run` opens a record for that piece of work and logs every command
it ran with its exit code. The dock above the composer shows **how many subtasks this
conversation ran** (and how many are running); one click on 展开 lists them — running ones
first, then finished ones with their result — and clicking a row opens its detail: the
terminal's full description, the result, and the commands. `subtask-done` writes the
result and decides the shell: `keepTerminal: true` (the default) leaves it idle for a
follow-up step, `false` closes a shell the tool opened. A terminal **you** opened is never
closed this way, and `close` is the other way to end one (it also refuses terminals the
tool did not open). The dock also lists the terminals **you** opened, labelled
用户建立的终端: one shows 使用中 while it is open and flips to 已结束 only once you close
it yourself. The records live in memory for the current DSH run — they describe this
conversation's work, and a restart clears them along with the terminals.

Terminals belong to the current DSH run — restarting DSH ends them — and the app can
re-create a browser terminal under a **new id**, so an id from an earlier answer may no
longer exist. The tool then falls back to one of its own shells and says which one it used.

Five things worth knowing:

- **A terminal you have open is read-only while the model works in it, and it stays
  read-only afterwards**: click **「接管输入」** in that terminal to type again. If you are
  typing when the model calls, the call is refused instead of landing in the middle of your
  line.
- **`read` returns the screen.** Anything that has scrolled away is gone, and
  full-screen programs (`vim`, `htop`) come back as their raw screen.
- **`run` needs a POSIX-style shell** (`sh`, `bash`, `zsh`). On `cmd.exe` or
  PowerShell, use `input`.
- **A busy terminal is never typed into.** If its prompt is not back — another command
  owns the foreground, and a `dsh` reply still streaming is one such command — `run` waits
  out its deadline and then declines instead of typing, so nothing is sent and the running
  command is not disturbed. Wait for it, type the command yourself in that terminal, or use a
  private shell for that work.
- **Long output is not thrown away.** A build or synthesis log's answer is at the
  bottom, so what comes back is the end of the output; the complete text is written
  to a file and the result names it.

Commands run as **you**, exactly as if you had typed them — and in a collaborative call you
see each one as a short, readable line (`__dsh_term_run 'make syn'`), because the first command
in that terminal defines the one-line helper there. What comes back is the output between its
two markers, plus the exit code. **There is no switch for this tool**: it is always available;
a tracked subtask runs in a private shell, a collaborative command runs in the terminal you
have open, and a named `id` decides explicitly. A destructive command still stops at the guard
unless the caller says it is intended.

Reach for it only when the work needs **one shell across several steps** — a long build worth
watching go by, an interactive program, a directory or environment that has to persist. For
everything self-contained the plain `wsl` tool is the better deal: a fresh shell per call runs
in parallel, needs no terminal at all, and never takes the keyboard away from you.

A distribution's files are reachable from Windows through `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...`, but
that share cannot be **written** through the platform's file tools: they publish a write by
renaming a temporary file into place, and that rename fails on the 9p share (`ENOTSUP`), while
the DACL copy they do first fails with `GetFileSecurityW EIO`. The path looks like a normal
Windows path and is not one, so these three tools run the same operations **inside** the
distribution instead — through the same launcher `wsl` uses, so there is no second transport
and no SMB, and they work on `/mnt/c/...` too.

```
wsl-read({ path: '~/project/src/main.js' })                    → the whole file
wsl-read({ path: '/var/log/syslog', offset: 200, limit: 40 })  → lines 200-239, and says so
wsl-write({ path: '~/notes/today.md', content: '…' })          → creates parents, replaces the file
wsl-edit({ path: '~/app/config.json', oldString: '"port": 80', newString: '"port": 8080' })

Ten things worth knowing:

- **`read` and `write` answer in the host's own words.** `wsl-read` returns the
  `<path>/<type>/<content>` envelope with numbered lines and the same `(End of file - total N
  lines)` and `(Showing lines a-b of N. Use offset=c to continue.)` footers as the platform's
  own `read`; `wsl-write` returns its `Created file` / `Updated file` acknowledgement. A model
  that has learned one format reads both without a second instruction. The **parameters** keep
  this plugin's camelCase (`path`, `oldString`) rather than the host's `file_path`/`old_string` —
  only the answer follows the host's shape. `wsl-edit` keeps its own one-line summary,
  `path  [2 replacements, 1.2 KB → 1.2 KB]`, because for a replacement the count and the size
  change are the two facts worth reporting.
- **A read declares a card for UIs that draw one.** The host's presentation vocabulary is
  declared with the result (numbered lines, the file's total, and a language hint taken from the
  extension — `python`, `typescript`, …), and stored with the result, so a client that renders
  it can redraw a replayed read without touching the distribution again. Whether a card is drawn
  is the client's decision: the bundled

Searches file contents inside the distribution and returns the matching lines grouped by file,
with line numbers — the same arguments and the same result shape as the platform's own `grep`
tool, pointed at a distribution instead of at Windows:

```
wsl-grep({ pattern: 'TODO', path: '~/project' })
wsl-grep({ pattern: 'listen\\(', path: '/etc/nginx', include: '*.conf' })
```

`pattern` is a regular expression, `path` is a Linux path (default: the session workspace), and
`include` is **one** positive glob of file NAMES (`*.ts`, `*.{js,jsx}`) — not a list, and negation
is not supported, because both engines take simple filters and a list would silently search the
wrong files. `{a,b}` alternation is the one list-like form accepted: it is expanded into one
simple filter per alternative, which is what the GNU `grep` fallback can actually run (it has no
brace shorthand, so passing the braces through would match no file at all). A glob with a path
separator (`sub/*.ts`, `**/*.ts`) is refused with a way forward: `rg --glob` reads it as a path
glob and `grep --include` looks at the base name only, so the same call would search different
files — narrow `path` instead. Results are capped at 250 matches with 2000 bytes per previewed
line; a capped result says how many were seen, and `wsl-read` on a matched file gives the
surrounding context. A result bigger than the 1 MiB body window is cut and reported as capped
rather than failing, and a tree where some files could not be read says the result is partial
instead of presenting what it found as complete. A single ma

The engine is whichever the distribution has: `rg` when it is installed (it honours
`.gitignore`, skips binaries, and reports JSON), and GNU `grep -E` otherwise, which is what
Ubuntu images ship. That difference is visible in two places, and worth knowing before you
write a pattern:

- **Dialect.** `\d` is the one shared escape GNU `grep -E` reads differently — as a literal `d`
  — so the fallback translates it to `[0-9]` (and `\D` to `[^0-9]`) before searching; `\w`,
  `\s` and `\b` are GNU extensions that mean the same in both engines. Anything only ripgrep
  understands (lookaround, backreferences) makes `grep` exit with an error, which is reported
  as a search failure rather than as "no matches".
- **Ignore rules.** `rg` skips what `.gitignore` excludes and `grep` does not, so the same
  search can return different sets of files on two machines. Install `ripgrep`
  (`wsl-bootstrap` will do it) when that difference matters — it is also what a distribution
  whose `grep` is busybox needs, because busybox grep has neither `-Z` nor `--include`; the
  tool probes for them and says so instead of failing with "invalid option".

A path containing a colon is why the fallback asks `grep` for `-Z`: the file name and the line
number are separated by a NUL byte, so `a:b.ts` stays one path instead of becoming `a` on line
`b.ts`. Binary files are never returned — `grep -I` and `rg`'s own default both skip them.

WSL's root does not need a password, so a single call can run as root (that is
`wsl -u root`). It is gated by a panel switch (「管理员模式（root）」, off by default):

```
wsl({ command: 'apt-get install -y jq', description: 'install jq', asRoot: true })
```

The switch is the authorisation, not the parameter: with it off, `asRoot: true` is
**refused and told which switch to turn on**, never quietly downgraded to your user
account. Every privileged result is marked (`[ran as root: wsl -u root]`), and the
destructive-command guard still applies on top: `rm -rf` needs `allowDangerous: true`
whether or not the call runs as root.

The four file tools take the same parameter and honour the same switch — `asRoot` on
`wsl-read`, `wsl-write`, `wsl-edit` and `wsl-grep` — so a file or a directory the user
cannot open is one argument away instead of one `wsl` call away:

```
wsl-read({ path: '/etc/ssl/private/site.key', asRoot: true })
wsl-grep({ pattern: 'PasswordAuthentication', path: '/etc/ssh', asRoot: true })
```

The published npm package is **`dsh-wsl-tool`**, not `dsh-wsl`: the registry
refuses `dsh-wsl` as too similar to the existing package `is-wsl`, and no token
or setting overrides that. The repository, the plugin and the market listing keep
the `dsh-wsl` name. The bundle patch points at its own entry by relative path, so
the folder under `node_modules` is free to differ — what has to match is the
specifier you install under.

1. Add the package to your DSH profile (`profiles/<profile>/package.json`):

```json
   { "dependencies": { "dsh-wsl-tool": "file:<path-to-this-repo>" } }
   ```

or run `dsh plugin add --profile <profile> dsh-wsl-tool` to install from npm,
   or `dsh plugin add --profile <profile> file:<path-to-this-repo>` from a
   checkout (which names the dependency after this package).

2. Nothing else. The package's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `tool-wsl` row
   itself when the bundle is loaded, process-wide, so the tools are
   available to every agent preset without further wiring. **There is no mode to
   pick and nothing to add to a preset** — the left-sidebar WSL panel arrives the
   same way.

Do **not** also list `tool-wsl` in a preset: DSH registers tools by name, and
   the second registration fails with
   `tool "wsl" is already registered in this scope`. One row, from the bundle.

3. Restart DSH.

The settings panel is the one optional piece: its form needs
`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, which most profiles already have (any plugin that
depends on it brings it in — add it to the profile's dependencies if yours does
not). Without it, the tools and the panel's 「WSL 终端启动路径」 field work
as usual and only the switches are absent — the panel says so instead of waiting
forever.

The manifest declares the DSH it needs — `"engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.1-rc.2" }`.
Two readers act on that declaration: the plugin market shows it as a requirement on
the entry and warns before an install onto an older host, and the host's own
install gate refuses a release whose declared range excludes the running DSH.
Only 0.2.1 and newer is supported: the pre-bridge terminal generation (DSH ≤0.2.0,
where a plugin could drive a browser terminal through `terminalController.follow` /
`write`) was removed, so the terminal tool reports that it cannot drive a terminal
on those hosts instead of reaching into the user's shell. The other five tools are
plain subprocess calls and still run there, but the package itself does not claim
that support.

Verified against DSH **0.2.1-rc.5** (and 0.2.1-rc.3 before it): the tool schemas pass DSH's own
`assertSupportedJsonSchema`, the subprocess seam is exercised against the real
provider rather than a shim, and the background-job path is checked against the
real job registry, including the session-id ownership fence (0.2.1 hands out
`kind-<16 hex>` job ids, so the check reads the registry's own id instead of
assuming a shape). `test/real-seam.mjs` is that check and it re-verifies a host in
about a minute, so point it at any DSH installation after an upgrade:

```sh
DSH_SUBPROCESS_LOCAL=/path/to/dsh/node_modules npm run test:real
```

A background job is owned by the calling session (`owner: exec.agent.id`), which
is what lets the model read it back with `job_output`/`job_kill` and what keeps
other sessions out; an execution with no agent starts the job unowned.

The terminal tool has two supported drives: the browser bridge (0.2.1: the
plugin's browser half joins a sidebar terminal the user opened, while the host
queues `attach`/`write`/`detach` over `/dsh-wsl-tool/term-bridge/poll` + `/events`
and the page answers with results, screen snapshots and output) and a private PTY
through `subprocess.spawnTerminal` for the tool's own work (same actions, same
records above the composer, a shell private to the tool, and a terminal you opened
left untouched). Both are checked by `npm test`.

The plugin ships a small client half: a **WSL** entry in the desktop app's left
sidebar, whose panel carries one switch per feature, each with a one-line
explanation.

| Switch | What it controls |
|---|---|
| `wsl` 命令执行 | registers the `wsl` tool |
| `wsl-path` 路径转换 | registers the `wsl-path` tool |
| `wsl-env` 能力体检 | registers the `wsl-env` tool |
| `wsl-doctor` 项目体检 | registers `wsl-doctor`. **Off by default**: the diagnostics tool is opt-in |
| `wsl-bootstrap` 安装工具链 | registers `wsl-bootstrap`, which may install into the distribution. **Off by default**, and its `dryRun` still has to be turned off per call |
| 后台任务 | whether `wsl` accepts `runInBackground` |
| 自动转换路径 | the default for the per-call `translatePaths` |
| 默认跟随会话工作区 | start in the session's directory instead of `~` when `workdir` is omitted. **On by default**: with it off, every relative path an agent writes lands in the Linux home, which is invisible from Explorer and grows the WSL disk image |
| Linux 默认工作目录 | a fixed Linux directory (for example `/mnt/d/project`) used when `workdir` is omitted. Filling it in wins over the switch above; clearing it falls back to `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR` when that is set, and otherwise to following the session |
| WSL 终端启动路径 | the optional sidebar terminal's startup directory — `--cd <dir>` on the `terminal-controller` row of your **profile patch** (see

The panel edits the plugin's own configuration, so the same values can be written
by hand (`- id: tool-wsl` with `config:` in a profile patch) or by environment
variables. `lib/config.js` owns the precedence — **plugin configuration, then the
environment, then the built-in defaults** — and a switch left at its default lets
the layer below decide. That is why `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR` keeps working for someone
who never opened the panel, including when the follow-session switch is still at
its ON default: an environment variable is an explicit deployment decision, so it
speaks louder than a switch default.

「WSL 终端启动路径」 is the one exception: the sidebar terminal belongs to another
plugin, so that field edits your profile's patch layer instead — the file is backed
up before every write, only the terminal row's `args` line is rewritten, and the
result is read back and undone if it is not exactly that one line.

**A change takes effect immediately**, tool switches included: registering a tool
returns its own disposer, so every settings update is diffed into the tool registry
and a switch flips the tool on or off in place — no restart, which matters because
the panel is where these get flipped. The one exception is 「WSL 终端启动路径」: it
edits another plugin's startup arguments in your profile patch, which that plugin
reads at boot, so that field applies after a restart. Distro and timeout are values
rather than features — set them in the patch or with `DSH_WSL_DISTRO` /
`DSH_WSL_TIMEOUT_MS`, and the panel shows what is currently in effect.

The settings surface needs `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, which the plugin declares as
an optional peer dependency: without it the tools still run on their defaults
and only the panel is missing.

At the bottom of the panel there is one feedback entry, next to it a short
submission guide, and — see [Feedback](#feedback) — a 「复制插件信息」 button. The
button asks the host half on `/dsh-wsl-tool/info` for this plugin's own facts (name,
version and repository read from its manifest, Node, platform), the DSH build it is
running inside, and the WSL facts `wsl-env` reports (default distribution, kernel,
capability flags) — then copies the result together with the effective
configuration. Nothing here is a string a release has to remember to edit, and a

- The sidebar's 新建终端 list is built from the composed `terminal-controller`
  row: it lists the configured `shell` first and keeps the shells it discovers
  (`powershell`, `cmd`, `bash`, …) selectable. The picker is core UI, so overriding

  plugin entry.
- No distribution is pinned, so `wsl.exe` follows the system default — the same
  rule the tools use when `DSH_WSL_DISTRO` is unset. Add `-d <name>` to `args` to
  pin one.
- The session workspace is a Windows path that `wsl.exe` translates, so the
  terminal opens in `/mnt/<drive>/…` exactly like the Windows shells do; and it is
  a real PTY (`xterm-256color`), so full-screen programs work.
- An id-targeted patch replaces that row's whole config, so restate anything else
  you had set on it (terminal limits, scrollback, a custom `shellCandidates` list).

The desktop app can be reached from a WSL prompt:

```sh
dsh -- "帮我把 nemu 的编译错误修掉"
```

The text goes into the DSH conversation the panel designates — the client shows the
same message and the same reply, live — and the terminal streams the turn back: a
thinking marker with its latency, the reasoning as the model produces it, the answer,
then a one-line summary (elapsed, steps, tokens). `Ctrl+C` stops waiting only; the
turn keeps running in the client.

The terminal is a second surface for that conversation: the text is forwarded verbatim,
and the client streams the reply back — a thinking timer, but no reasoning text. When
already answering, the line is steered into the live turn instead of queueing, so the
same agent reacts immediately and nothing is dropped.

| command | does |
|---|---|
| `dsh -- "问题"` | send to the current session and stream the reply (`--` marks a message; unquoted words after it work too) |
| `dsh <id> -- "问题"` | send to that session |
| `dsh list` | sessions, newest first; `*` marks the current one |
| `dsh new <id>` | create a session (it appears in the client) and switch to it |
| `dsh use <id>` | switch the current session |
| `dsh rm <id>` | archive a session — the client's own reversible remove |
| `dsh status` | current session and channel state |

A message needs the `--` marker; a bare first word is read as a **command**, so a typo such as `dsh statsu` exits with `不存在此命令` (no such command) and the usage hint instead of being sent to the model. That is why the marker exists: the shell removes quotes before the shim runs, so "was it quoted" cannot be answered — `--` can.

Messages typed in the terminal arrive in the conversation marked **【WSL 终端】**, so a terminal turn is never mistaken for something typed in the client, and the ⏱ thinking clock keeps ticking while the model works instead of freezing at its first number — it reads in minutes and seconds (`0分05秒`, then `1分23秒`). The shim resolves its transport once per channel start (it used to probe the blocked path on every command), and from the moment the Host accepts the request it shows a live **… 已送达，等待模型 Ns** clock — so the wait is visible instead of looking frozen. That wait is the model, not the channel: measured on the same machine the Host acknowledges in ~2–20 ms and the shim adds ~0.1 s, while one turn took ~1.8 s on a small conversation and ~4.8 s on the panel landing that carried ~182 k input tokens. When the turn finishes, the terminal prints the signed-in DeepSeek account balance (recharge and bonus wallets, formatted like the account panel). A signed-out or unavailable account is reported as such instead of `¥0.00`, and the wallet is fetched in the background while the model works, so the line costs the reply nothing. If terminal chat feels slow, give it a dedicated lean conversatio

A `dsh -- "…"` aimed at the very conversation whose tool call is running it cannot be sent: the prompt would join that live turn, whose end waits for the command to return — a self-lock. The channel refuses it and says why instead of hanging until the deadline; wait for the turn, or type it in the client. The shim passes its caller session (`x-dsh-wsl-caller`) only when the plugin's terminal tool started that shell, so a person typing at a terminal is never affected.

While a turn streams, the terminal has no prompt — but it is still yours: press Enter once and the answer is held back (the live clock stops painting, the input line is clean), type the message, press Enter again and it is delivered to the same conversation as a steer, after which the answer resumes (`已插入当前对话，继续输出`). A second empty Enter cancels. Set `DSH_WSL_NO_STEER=1` to turn that reader off (scripts and pipes never get it; only a real terminal does).

A terminal prompt is **nothing but the message you typed** — the screen never appears in the transcript. What you were looking at still reaches the model: the Host asks the page's terminal bridge which sidebar terminal is running that command, captures the newest hundred lines of its screen (read-only), and hands them to the model as **hidden runtime context on its next request** (the same `systemPrompt` context mechanism the working-directory and memory plugins use; it is consumed once and never stored in the conversation). Need more than that? The model can read the same terminal with this plugin's own terminal tool (`wsl-term read`, read-only). It is best effort and bounded — no open DSH window, no matching terminal, or a slow attach simply means no context, and the turn is never delayed by more than ~3 s. A prompt that came from a tool call gets no context: nobody typed it at a screen.

Set it up once in the panel: turn on **启用 dsh 命令** and click **安装 dsh 命令** — the default landing is the most recently active conversation — the one you are looking at (pick another from the list, or create one right there, if you want a different landing); the shim lands in `~/.local/bin/dsh`. After that the plugin keeps it healthy by itself: on every start (and settings change) it reads the installed shim and, when it is missing or older than the running version, installs it again without asking — the check costs one `cat`, it never touches the distro while the channel is off or while a turn is streaming, and `autoInstallShim: false` in the plugin config turns it off. The plugin binds a small HTTP
server to the address WSL uses as its default gateway, on a random port, and demands
the token it generated at mount on every request. The desktop has to be running, and
the designated conversation is ordinary: the channel admits a normal user message (prefixed
with 「【WSL 终端】」), so
the same reply appears in the client.

| Param | Required | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | yes | string | Linux command to execute |
| `description` | yes | string | short UI label |
| `workdir` | no | string | Linux path (`/home/me`, `~/src`) or Windows path, default `~` |
| `timeoutMs` | no | number | timeout in milliseconds, default 600000 (10 min); the process is killed and the result marked as timed out |
| `distro` | no | string | WSL distribution; defaults to the system default distribution |
| `env` | no | object | extra environment variables to export (keys must be valid shell names) |
| `stdin` | no | string | text written to the command stdin (UTF-8) before it runs |
| `runInBackground` | no | boolean | run as a job and return its id immediately; read with `job_output`, stop with `job_kill` |
| `allowDangerous` | no | boolean | set `true` to run destructive commands |
| `asRoot` | no | boolean | run this call as root (`wsl -u root`); refused unless the panel's 管理员模式 switch is on |
| `translatePaths` | no | boolean | default `true`; set `false` to pass `command` through verbatim |

The panel's switches and value fields (`tools.wsl`, `tools.path`, `tools.env`,
`tools.doctor`, `tools.bootstrap`, `tools.read`, `tools.write`, `tools.edit`, `tools.grep`,
`backgroundJobs`, `translatePaths`, `startInSessionWorkspace`, `workdir`, `dangerGuard`,
`allowRoot`, `distro`, `timeoutMs`) live in the profile patch and take effect as described on
each row.
Two of them have no environment variable on purpose: `dangerGuard` (its OFF
position is the footgun) and `allowRoot` (WSL's root needs no password, so the
switch IS the authorisation). The environment layer:
| Environment variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_WSL_DISTRO` | (system default) | Pin the distribution for every call. |
| `DSH_WSL_TIMEOUT_MS` | `600000` | Default deadline for a model-issued command; `timeoutMs` overrides it per call. |
| `DSH_WSL_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` | `86400000` | Ceiling for a per-call `timeoutMs`, mirroring the platform shell tools' `maxTimeoutMs`. The default deadline obeys it too. |
| `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR` | (unset: follow the switch) | Where a call starts without a `workdir`: `home` (the Linux `~`), `session` (the session working directory, i.e. `/mnt/<drive>/...` for a Windows checkout),

An unparsable or out-of-range value falls back to the default: one bad variable
must not take every tool down. Values are read once per mount, so a change
takes effect on restart.

- Each call runs in a fresh shell — no cwd/variables/functions persist between calls.
- **stdin is `/dev/null` unless you pass `stdin`.** An interactive command (`read`,
  `cat`, a `sudo` password prompt without `-S`) otherwise gets EOF immediately and
  cannot wait for input; nothing in this plugin can prompt. A password passed via
  `stdin` is recorded in the session transcript.
- With nothing configured a call starts in the session's working directory (the
  follow-session switch is on by default). Set `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR=home` to start in
  `~` instead, `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR=session` to say so explicitly, or an explicit path
  for a fixed directory (see Configuration).
- The distro is the caller's `distro`, else `DSH_WSL_DISTRO`, else the system
  default; there is no hardcoded fallback name.
- An unknown distro is reported as a clear error (`distribution "X" is not registered`) instead of a raw `-1` exit code, and any other launcher failure (`Wsl/Service/WSL_E_*`) is surfaced with its code rather than passed off as the command's own exit status.
- **A background job outlives the call.** `runInBackground: true` returns a job id (`wsl-N`) immediately and registers the work with the host

```
  [stdout truncated: at most the last 65536 of 1288895 bytes were kept; full stream: C:\...\stdout.log]
  ```
- **Host shell facts are forwarded into the distro**, because WSL does not pass Windows environment variables across on its own: `DSH_SESSION_ID`, `DSH_SHELL` and `DSH_HOME` (translated to its `/mnt/...` view) are exported ahead of the command, so a script sees the same session facts the platform's own shell tools inject. They are resolved **per call** from the host's `shellEnv` registry — the same source the other shell tools read — because they are session-scoped, not host constants; reading the host's own `process.env` finds nothing and silently forwards nothing. **`DSH_WEB_URL` is deliberately not forwarded** — it is a `127.0.0.1` URL for the Windows-side server, and in the default NAT networking mode WSL cannot reach Windows loopback (measured: HTTP 000 on both `127.0.0.1` and the host IP, which the server does not bind either). An explicit `env` entry always overrides a forwarded one.
- `timeoutMs` defaults to 10 minutes so a wedged `wsl.exe` cannot hang the call forever; pass a larger value for genuinely long work, up to the `DSH_WSL_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` ceiling (24 h

```
  workspace: /mnt/d/DSHworkarea (Windows drive mount /mnt/d — builds, installs and git are much slower here; prefer a path under /home when it matters)
  ```

It is worth believing. Measured on the author's machine: a 128 MB sequential write
  ran at ~2.1 GB/s on ext4 against ~247 MB/s on `/mnt/d`, and creating 400 small
  files took under 10 ms against 0.72 s (a later re-run: 885 vs 116 MB/s, and 13 ms
  against 745 ms — the ratios hold at roughly 8× and 50×).

It is not only slower. `/mnt/<drive>` is a 9p (drvfs) mount, so it keeps **Windows**
  filesystem semantics: `chmod`/`chown` do not stick (a `chmod 600` reads back as
  `777`), names are case-insensitive (so a case-sensitive import only fails on Linux
  CI), symlinks and the executable bit are synthetic, and **inotify does not work at
  all** — a watcher inside the distro receives no events for writes from either side
  (measured with an inotify probe on `/mnt/d`: zero events for a Windows-side write
  and for a Linux-side write, while the same probe on ext4 reported create, modify
  and close-write). Dev servers, `--watch` modes and file-watching tests are
  therefore blind on a Windows drive. Keep a project under `/home` when it matters:
  it recovers real semantics, real watch events, and the speed above.
- Destructive commands are refused unless the call passes `allowDangerous: true`:
  - **any recursive delete** — `rm -r`, `rm -rf`, `rm -r -f`, `rm -R --force`, `rm --recursive` — because with stdin on `/dev/null` nothing prompts, so `rm -r tree` deletes silently. Each `rm` invocation is judged on its own command segment, so `rm a -f; rm b -r` cannot combine into a pass; an `rm

DSH's file sandbox is enforced at two points: the shell executors
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-sandbox`, `-pwsh-sandbox`, which wrap the exact argv
through `ctx.sandbox`) and the filesystem service (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-sandbox`,
a policy fence on the two mutations). **`wsl` is in neither.** It spawns
`wsl.exe` through the host `subprocess` service, below that layer, so a
`workspace-write` policy does not confine it: it can write anywhere the Linux
side can, and anywhere under `/mnt/<drive>` that Windows permits.

That is not a gap this plugin can close by "joining" the sandbox. On Windows the
sandbox resolves to an ACL / restricted-token runner, while the file work happens
inside the Linux kernel: a write to `/home/...` touches the distro's own
filesystem image, which no Windows token constrains, and a write to `/mnt/c/...`
travels through the filesystem bridge, where ACL enforcement is not something to
rely on. Wrapping `wsl.exe` would confine the launcher, not the writes — and a
false sense of isolation is worse than a documented absence. (The platform's own
`dsh-fs-sandbox` is candid about its own limits too: "containment, not a security
boundary".)

What `wsl` does have is the destructive-command guard described above: a
deterministic refusal list, not a kernel boundary. Treat this tool as able to
touch anything your WSL installation can, and grant it accordingly.

The package declares a `dsh.bundle` manifest (see `package.json`), so once the
repository is listed it can be installed by name, e.g.
`dsh plugin add dsh-wsl-tool`, and storefronts will offer it for one-click
install. Installing from a local path (`file:`) as shown above keeps working
either way.

The plugin is a cordis module that injects the host-plane `tools` and
`subprocess` registries. `index.js` is only the entry point; the implementation
is split by concern:

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `lib/config.js` | Defaults and environment overrides, resolved once per mount. |
| `lib/paths.js` | Shell quoting and Windows -> WSL path translation. |
| `lib/guard.js` | The destructive-command rules. |
| `lib/result.js` | Launcher-noise filters, truncation facts, marker rendering. |
| `lib/diagnostics.js` | The `wsl-env` capability probe, its parser and its lines. |
| `lib/runner.js` | The single spawn path plus launcher-error classification. |
| `lib/tools/*.js` | The tool definitions (schema, execute, presentCall). |
| `lib/doctor.js` | The project probe for `wsl-doctor`: one shell script, its parser, the report composer. |
| `lib/bootstrap.js` | The recipes, plan builder and outcome rendering for `wsl-bootstrap`. |
| `lib/terminal.js` | The text and selection work behind `wsl-term`: escape stripping, command markers, terminal picking. |

- `apply()` resolves the configuration and registers the enabled tools, each with a
  JSON-schema parameter definition, an output schema, a `render` hook and an
  async `execute`.
- Every call goes through one spawn path (`runner.runWsl`): `wsl.exe -d <distro>
  -e bash -lc "<exports; cd workdir && command>"` through the host `subprocess`
  service, with stdout/stderr capped at the configured window (spilling to disk
  up to 64 MiB), a 3 s grace period after abort, and a deadline that defaults to
  10 minutes. The plugin's own probes get a 30 s ceiling so a wedged WSL service
  cannot hang a tool call forever.
- `env` entries are exported at the front of the command so they reach the
  Linux side reliably; Windows drive paths are rewritten to `/mnt/...` before
  the command is built.
- Output is returned as `{ exitCode, signal, timedOut, timeoutMs, truncated,
  stdout, stderr, stdoutTotalBytes, stdoutDroppedBytes, stderrTotalBytes,
  stderrDroppedBytes, stdoutSpillPath, stderrSpillPath, jobId }`; the `render` hook
  formats it into text with the markers listed above. The truncation marker
  quotes the window size rather than a count derived from the decoded text,
  which can be off

The plugin publishes no services of its own and is inserted process-wide by its own
bundle patch, so it needs no realm — and no preset entry either.

The plugin is plain ESM with no build step or runtime dependencies outside the
DSH host plane. Iterate by pointing a profile dependency at the checkout:

```json
{ "dependencies": { "dsh-wsl-tool": "file:/path/to/dsh-wsl" } }
```

then restart DSH and call the tools from **any** session: the bundle patch registers
them process-wide, so no preset declares the row.

```sh
npm test          # 1579 host checks against real WSL (shim for ctx.subprocess) + 305 client checks
npm run test:real # the same checks against the REAL provider, plus the seam-fact suite
```

`npm test` substitutes only `ctx.subprocess`, with a shim that reproduces the
seam's bounded tail windows, spill files and termination ladder, and drives the
the tools against the real WSL installation. It covers path translation,
workdir quoting, the destructive guard, distro selection, exit-code/timeout/
truncation markers, `wsl-path`, `wsl-env`, argument validation, configuration
parsing, launcher-error classification, the returned shape against each declared
`output.schema`, and a token budget for the model-facing catalog.

`npm run test:real` runs that same suite against `LocalSubprocessRuntime` — the
shim must not drift from the real seam — and then `test/real-seam.mjs`, which
checks the facts a shim cannot vouch for (that `readFrom(0).nextOffset` is the
whole-stream total, that the spill file holds the complete stream, that a
timeout really kills the Linux side of `wsl.exe`) and validates every published
schema with DSH's own `assertSupportedJsonSchema`. It needs a DSH installation:

```sh
DSH_SUBPROCESS_LOCAL=/path/to/dsh/node_modules npm run test:real
```

A `file:` dependency is a **copy**, so editing this checkout does not change what
DSH loads. After any change:

```sh
npm run sync                  # copies into ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-wsl
npm run sync -- /path/to/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/<your-key>
```

The target must be the folder your profile's dependency key created (the default
above is this checkout's own key); the plugin loads its entry by relative path, so
the folder name itself never matters.

then restart DSH — the plugin is imported once at load.

面向模型（model-facing）的 **WSL** 工具插件，用于 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）。它让智能体直接通过
`wsl.exe` 执行 Linux 命令——无需手写 `.sh` 脚本或 `pwsh` 包装——并且在**命令执行**这一层基本对齐
Linux 原生 DSH：真实的 Linux 内核与 bash、退出码与信号、超时、截断与落盘、可用内置 job 工具读回的
后台作业、stdin，以及 Windows/WSL 路径自动转换。

它也能像你一样地干活：在**一个能保持状态的 shell** 里，一件事一个 shell，每条命令都连同退出码留下记录，
输入框上方只显示一行紧凑的子任务数量；当你**点名自己打开的终端**时，键盘点一下就能拿回来。

有两点限制值得在依赖它之前知道：`wsl` 调用位于 DSH 沙箱层之下，文件策略约束不到它
（见[沙箱边界](#沙箱边界)）；项目放在 Windows 盘上时仍是 **Windows** 的文件系统语义——没有 POSIX
权限位、文件名大小写不敏感、收不到文件变更通知——速度也低一个数量级（见[注意事项](#注意事项)）。

| 工具 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `wsl` | 执行 Linux 命令，返回带退出码、超时与截断标记的 `stdout`/`stderr` |
| `wsl-path` | 通过 `wslpath` 在 Windows 与 WSL 路径间互转 |
| `wsl-env` | 汇总 WSL 环境（发行版、内核、CPU、内存、磁盘） |
| `wsl-doctor` | 对照项目清单与发行版实际能力，指出缺什么——包括那些其实是 Windows 二进制的命令。只读，**默认关**（需要诊断时再开） |
| `wsl-bootstrap` | 按固定配方在发行版里补装缺失的工具链，先出计划再动手 |
| `wsl-term` | 在本会话的终端里工作：一件事一个 shell，每件事都在输入框上方留下记录 |
| `wsl-read` | 读取发行版里的文本文件，整份或按行范围；二进制与非 UTF-8 直接拒绝 |
| `wsl-write` | 写入发行版里的文本文件，原子替换，父目录自动创建 |
| `wsl-edit` | 在发行版里的文件中替换唯一匹配的字符串 |
| `wsl-grep` | 在发行版里按正则搜索文件内容，按文件分组返回带行号的匹配行 |

执行形式：

```
wsl.exe [-d <distro>] -e bash -lc "cd <workdir> && <command>"
```

返回 `stdout`/`stderr`，并附加 `[exit code: N]` / `[killed by signal: ...]` /
`[timed out after Nms; the command was killed]` / `[output truncated: ...]` 标记。

`<distro>` 取调用参数 `distro`，其次 `DSH_WSL_DISTRO`，都没有时**完全不传 `-d`**，
由 `wsl.exe` 使用**系统默认发行版**——这正是本插件能装到没有 `Ubuntu-22.04` 的机器上的原因。

超过 Windows 命令行上限（32767 字符）的脚本会改为通过 **stdin** 交给
`wsl.exe [-d <distro>] -e bash -ls` 执行，因此长命令没有体积上限。

传 `stdin` 可以把文本喂给命令（默认是 `/dev/null`，交互式命令会立刻 EOF）；传
`runInBackground: true` 则把命令交给宿主的任务注册表，模型随后用**已有的**
**`job_output`** 工具读它、用 **`job_kill`** 停它——不需要任何新工具。后台任务需要
preset 组合里有 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs`；没有时会直接报错说明，而不是悄悄退化成
前台执行。

双向转换路径：`C:\Users\me\a.txt` → `/mnt/c/Users/me/a.txt`，或
`/home/me/a.txt` → `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-22.04\home\me\a.txt`。方向自动识别，
也可用 `direction: 'win' | 'linux'` 强制指定。

返回发行版列表、被探测的发行版、内核与架构、CPU 数、内存与磁盘占用，以及这台机器
**实际能做什么**：

```
distro: Ubuntu-22.04 (system default)
Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64
nproc: 24
Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS · WSL2 · cgroup v2

让智能体在动手前就知道有什么可用：WSL1 还是 WSL2、服务是否由 systemd 托管、cgroup 版本
（容器相关）、GPU 直通、docker（未装／只有 CLI／守护进程版本）、挂载了哪些盘，以及
`/etc/wsl.conf` 与 Windows 侧 `.wslconfig` 的配置。可传可选参数 `distro`。

每一项都是可选的，且如实降级：探针没跑成的行会被省略，读到了但为空的值会写明
（`docker: not installed`、`.wslconfig: not set`），探测失败会写进摘要而不是被丢掉，
发行版不存在则直接报错，而不是给出一份残缺答案。注意 `wsl --version` 输出是**本地化**的，
因此其标签按启动器原样透传、不按名称解析；Direct3D/MSRDC/DXCore 版本作为噪声被省略。

回答一个项目自己的 README 答不了的问题：**这份代码指望的工具链，在这套发行版里真的能用吗？**
它读取目录里的清单（`package.json` 与各种 lockfile、`.nvmrc`、`tsconfig.json`、`Cargo.toml`、
`go.mod`、`pyproject.toml`、`requirements.txt`、`Dockerfile`、`docker-compose.yml`、`Makefile`、
`CMakeLists.txt`），然后逐项给出它在 Linux 侧的位置：

```
distro: Ubuntu-22.04 (system default)
workspace: /mnt/d/proj (Windows drive mount /mnt/d — builds, installs and git are much slower here; …)
project: package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml

那行 `WINDOWS` 就是它存在的理由。WSL 会把 Windows 的 `PATH` 接到 Linux 的后面，于是
`npm` 在一套**根本没有 `node`** 的发行版里"找得到"（本机实测就是
`/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/npm`），模型拿它去跑 Linux 目录时报的错两头都不沾。整体只读、
开销很小，值得在把失败归咎于命令本身之前先跑一次。可选参数 `workspace`（Linux 目录；默认取
配置的目录，否则取会话工作区）与 `distro`。

**在发行版内部**补装缺失的工具链，只认固定配方：`node`（Node.js LTS 装进 `/usr/local`，
校验 sha256，并启用 corepack）、`pnpm`、`python`（python3 + pip + venv）、`build`
（build-essential）、`tools`（jq、rsync、curl、git、ca-certificates）。依赖按需带上：
`pnpm` 会带上 `node`，`curl` 缺失时 `node` 会带上 `tools`。

**它默认关**，且 `dryRun` 默认为 `true`，所以第一次调用只打印计划、什么都不改：

```
dry run — nothing has been installed (distro Ubuntu-22.04)

already present:
  python — python3, pip and venv (apt)

已经满足的配方会被跳过；计划里包含 apt 自己会做什么，因此安装前就能看到具体改动。安装以 root 执行；
某一步失败即停下并附上它的输出末尾。

这里其他工具都是**每次调用开一个全新 shell**，这让它们可以安全并行，也是默认方式。`wsl-term` 反过来：
**一件事一个 shell**。它适合那些"shell 自身状态就是重点"的活——想看着它跑完的构建、交互式程序、
必须在多步之间保留的目录或环境。

`wsl-term` 就在这个终端里工作：

```
wsl-term({ action: "list" })                                  → 有哪些终端
wsl-term({ action: "read" })                                  → 当前屏幕
wsl-term({ action: "run", command: "make sta", subtask: "跑通 sta 流程" })
                                                              → 在那个终端里执行，返回输出与退出码

**它驱动哪个 shell：两条规则，区别在 `subtask` 参数。**

- **带 `subtask` 的 `run` 是「被记录的任务」。** 它用**工具自己开的私有 WSL shell**：一件事一个 shell，
  每条命令记在输入框上方，`subtask-done` 决定闲置还是关掉它。它不在侧边栏里，只有工具往里打字——
  子任务的管理动作永远不碰你打开的终端。
- **不带 `subtask` 的命令是「终端协作」。** `run`、`read`、`input`、`interrupt` 使用**你开着的那个最新终端**，
  命令在你眼前执行、屏幕你随时能读；工具工作期间它是只读的，点 **「接管输入」** 就能继续输入。
  工具**永远不会关闭**你打开的终端。
- **显式点名 `id` 的调用最优先**，不管那是不是你开的终端。

如果你一个终端都没开，不带 `subtask` 的命令也会开一个私有 shell——那是本会话可用的 shell，但**不会出现在侧边栏**。
协作这一半靠桥接实现：从 DSH 0.2.1 起宿主不再允许插件直接附着浏览器终端，但本插件自己的**浏览器半**运行在页面里，
那个附着在页面里是允许的，于是宿主把 `attach`/`write`/`detach` 命令经两条同源路由交给它（不额外开端口、不额外起服务）。
旧代宿主（≤0.2.0）已不受支持：终端工具会明确报告无法驱动，而不是通过 `follow`/`write` 直接操作你的终端。

readme.section: 每件事都留下一条记录
readme.text:
在 `run` 上给出 `subtask`，就会为这件事开一条记录，并记下它跑过的每条命令和退出码。输入框上方的显示默认只写
**这次对话跑过多少个子任务**（以及几个还在运行）；点一下 **展开** 才会列出来：**正在运行的排在最上面**，已经结束的
带着结果排在后面；再点开一行会看到详情——终端的完整描述、结果、以及每条命令。`subtask-done` 负责写下结果并决定
这个 shell 的去留：`keepTerminal: true`（默认）把它闲置着等你下一步，`false` 则关掉**工具自己开的**那个 shell；
**你自己开的终端永远不会被这样关掉**，要关就用 `close`（它同样拒绝关闭不是工具开的终端）。
dock 里也会列出**你打开的终端**，标注为「用户建立的终端」：开着的时候显示「使用中」，只有**你自己关掉**它之后才变成「已结束」。
这些记录只存在**本次 DSH 运行**的内存里：它们描述的是这次对话做过的事，重启会连同终端一起清空。

readme.section: 每件事都留下一条记录
readme.text:
终端属于**本次 DSH 运行**，重启即结束；应用在重新创建浏览器终端时会给它一个**新的 id**，所以早前消息里的 id
可能已经不存在——这时工具会退到它自己的某个 shell，并说明用了哪一个。

用之前有几点要知道：

readme.section: 每件事都留下一条记录
readme.text:
- **你开着的终端在模型工作期间是只读的，而且之后仍然只读**：点那个终端里的 **「接管输入」** 才能继续输入。
  你正在打字时模型发起的调用会被拒绝，不会插进你那半行命令里。
- **`read` 返回的是屏幕内容**：已经滚出去的内容取不回来；`vim`、`htop` 这类全屏程序返回的是它们的原始屏幕。
- **`run` 需要 POSIX 风格的 shell**（`sh`、`bash`、`zsh`）；`cmd.exe` 或 PowerShell 下请用 `input`。
- **忙碌中的终端绝不会被写入。** 如果提示符还没回来——另一个命令占着前台，正在流式输出回复的 `dsh` 就是这种情况——`run` 会等到期限后**拒绝输入**，什么都不发，正在跑的命令不受打扰。等它结束、在那个终端里自己输入，或者改用私有 shell。
- **长输出不会丢。** 构建与综合日志的结论在末尾，所以返回的是输出的**末尾部分**；完整内容会写入文件，
  结果里给出该文件的路径。

readme.section: 每件事都留下一条记录
readme.text:
命令以**你的身份**运行，和你自己敲完全一样；在**协作调用**里每条命令在终端中都是**一行短而可读**的样子
（`__dsh_term_run 'make syn'`）——因为工具第一次在那个终端里跑命令时，会先定义好这个一行的包装函数。
拿回来的是两个标记之间的输出，外加退出码。**这个工具没有开关**：它一直在；带 `subtask` 的跑在私有 shell 里，
不带 `subtask` 的在**你开着的终端**里协作执行，显式点名 `id` 则按点名来。危险命令仍然要先过守卫（除非调用方
明确说明那是有意为之）。

它只在**需要同一个 shell 跨多步**时才值得用 —— 想看着它跑完的长构建、交互式程序、必须保留的目录或环境。
自洽的命令交给 `wsl` 更划算：每次全新 shell、可以并行、根本不需要终端，也不会把键盘从你手里拿走。

发行版里的文件在 Windows 侧可以通过 `\\wsl.localhost\<发行版>\...` 访问，但那是个 **9p 共享，写不进去**：
平台的读写工具靠"先写临时文件再改名"来保证原子性，而这个改名在 9p 上直接失败（`ENOTSUP`），
它之前那次 DACL 复制则报 `GetFileSecurityW EIO`。这个路径看起来像 Windows 路径，其实不是，
所以这三个工具改成**在发行版内部**完成同样的操作——走的是 `wsl` 用的同一个启动器，
没有第二套传输、不依赖 SMB，`/mnt/c/...` 上的文件一样能读写。

```
wsl-read({ path: '~/project/src/main.js' })                    → 整份文件
wsl-read({ path: '/var/log/syslog', offset: 200, limit: 40 })  → 第 200-239 行，返回时标明是这一段
wsl-write({ path: '~/notes/today.md', content: '…' })          → 自动建父目录，整文件替换
wsl-edit({ path: '~/app/config.json', oldString: '"port": 80', newString: '"port": 8080' })

有几点要知道：

- **`read` 和 `write` 的回答沿用平台自己的格式。** `wsl-read` 返回
  `<path>/<type>/<content>` 信封，行号在前，结尾是平台 `read` 那句 `(End of file - total N
  lines)` 或 `(Showing lines a-b of N. Use offset=c to continue.)`；`wsl-write` 返回它的
  `Created file` / `Updated file` 回执。模型学会一种格式，两种世界都读得懂。**参数名**保持本插件
  的 camelCase（`path`、`oldString`），并不改成平台的 `file_path`/`old_string`——只有"回答"跟平台
  对齐。`wsl-edit` 保留自己那行摘要 `path  [2 replacements, 1.2 KB → 1.2 KB]`：替换这件事，
  值得知道的就是"改了几处"和"文件变成了多大"。
- **读的时候会声明一张供界面用的卡片。** 行号、文件总行数、按扩展名推断的语言提示（`python`、
  `typescript`……）都随结果存下，读得到这份元数据的客户端重放时不必再碰发行版里的文件；画不画卡片
  是客户端自己的决定——**自带的 Web 界面目前显示的是纯编号文本**（它的工具卡片由客户端插件按自己的
  工具名注册）。模型读到的始终是上面那个信封。
- **只处理文本，而且会明说。** 二进制文件、或不是合法 UTF-8 的文件会被**拒绝**并给出原因，而不是把乱码
  当内容返回。这类事情交给 `wsl`（`base64`、`od`、`cp`），它也是这三个工具覆盖不到时的出口。
- **单行超过读取窗口会被拒绝，而不是分页到永远。** `wsl-read` 每次最多返回 1 MiB，而窗口是按行分的，
  所以一整行超过这个额度（压缩过的 JSON、打包脚本）根本没法按行翻页：调用会直接说明并指向 `wsl`
  工具（`head -c`、`fold`、`cut`），而不是一直回答 `Showing lines 1-0`。
- **写入是原子的、保留权限、并跟随符号链接。** 内容先写进同目录的临时文件，再改名覆盖目标，所以写到
  一半中断也不会毁掉原文件；写之前会复制原文件的权限（`chmod --reference` 不可用时退回 `stat -c %a`，
  两者都失败则**报错**而不是悄悄把 `755` 脚本改成 `600`）；通过符号链接写入会改**链接指向的目标**，
  而不是把链接本身替换成普通文件。只替换**普通文件**：FIFO、socket、设备节点会被拒绝（`is not a
  regula

在发行版里搜索文件内容，按文件分组返回带行号的匹配行——参数和结果形状都与平台自带的 `grep` 一致，
只是指向发行版而不是 Windows：

```
wsl-grep({ pattern: 'TODO', path: '~/project' })
wsl-grep({ pattern: 'listen\\(', path: '/etc/nginx', include: '*.conf' })
```

`pattern` 是正则，`path` 是 Linux 路径（默认当前会话的工作目录），`include` 是**一个**按"文件名"匹配的
正向 glob（`*.ts`、`*.{js,jsx}`），不是列表，也不支持取反——两个引擎都只接受简单过滤条件，传列表只会
静默地搜错文件。`{a,b}` 交替是唯一允许的"类列表"写法：它会被展开成每个分支一个过滤条件，因为 GNU
`grep` 回退没有花括号语法，原样传过去会把所有文件都过滤掉。带路径分隔符的 glob（`sub/*.ts`、
`**/*.ts`）会被拒绝并给出替代做法：`rg --glob` 按路径匹配、`grep --include` 只看文件名，同一个调用
在两个引擎上会搜不同的文件——请改用收窄的 `path`。结果上限 250 条匹配、每条预览行 2000 字节；被截断
时结果会说明一共看到多少条，需要上下文就用 `wsl-read` 读那个文件。结果超过 1 MiB 正文窗口时会被截断
并标记为截断（而不是报错），有文件读不到时结果会明确标注不完整，而不是把找到的部分当作全部；若单条匹配的
那一行本身超过窗口（压缩文件常见），会明确报错而不是回答"没有匹配"——那条匹配是真的，用 `wsl` 的
`grep -o`/`rg -o` 去查它。

引擎取决于发行版里装了什么：有 `rg` 就用 `rg`（尊重 `.gitignore`、跳过二进制、输出 JSON），否则退回
GNU `grep -E`——Ubuntu 镜像默认就是后者。这个差异在两处可见，写正则前值得知道：

- **方言。** `\d` 是两个引擎里唯一含义不同的公共转义（GNU `grep -E` 把它当字面 `d`），所以回退方案
  会先把它翻成 `[0-9]`（`\D` 翻成 `[^0-9]`）再搜；`\w`、`\s`、`\b` 是 GNU 扩展，两边含义一致。
  只有 `rg` 认得的写法（环视、反向引用）会让 `grep` 直接报错，结果是**搜索失败**，而不是"没有匹配"。
- **忽略规则。** `rg` 会跳过 `.gitignore` 排除的文件，`grep` 不会，所以同一条搜索在两台机器上
  可能返回不同的文件集合。在意这个差异时，用 `wsl-bootstrap` 把 `ripgrep` 装上——`grep` 是 busybox
  版本的发行版（Alpine 等）也只能靠它：busybox grep 没有 `-Z` 和 `--include`，工具会先探测并说明，
  而不是把 "invalid option" 当成搜索失败。

路径里带冒号正是回退方案要向 `grep` 要 `-Z` 的原因：文件名与行号之间用 NUL 分隔，`a:b.ts` 就还是
一个路径，而不会被拆成"文件 `a`、第 `b.ts` 行"。二进制文件不会出现在结果里——`grep -I` 与 `rg`
的默认行为都会跳过它们。

WSL 的 root 不需要密码，因此可以让单次调用以 root 执行（即 `wsl -u root`）。它由面板里的一项开关把关
（「管理员模式（root）」，默认关）：

```
wsl({ command: 'apt-get install -y jq', description: 'install jq', asRoot: true })
```

授权来自开关而不是参数：开关关着时，`asRoot: true` 会被**明确拒绝并告知该打开哪个开关**，而不是悄悄降级成
你的普通用户。每次以 root 执行的结果都会标注（`[ran as root: wsl -u root]`）；危险命令守卫照旧叠加生效：
`rm -rf` 无论是否以 root 执行都仍需 `allowDangerous: true`。

四个文件工具接受同一个参数、遵守同一项开关——`wsl-read`、`wsl-write`、`wsl-edit`、`wsl-grep` 都支持
`asRoot`——所以"用户打不开的文件或目录"只差一个参数，不必再绕去写一条 `wsl` 命令：

```
wsl-read({ path: '/etc/ssl/private/site.key', asRoot: true })
wsl-grep({ pattern: 'PasswordAuthentication', path: '/etc/ssh', asRoot: true })
```

发布到 npm 的包名是 **`dsh-wsl-tool`**，不是 `dsh-wsl`：registry 判定 `dsh-wsl` 与既有包
`is-wsl` 过于相似而拒绝，换 token 或改设置都无法绕过。仓库名、插件名与市场条目仍沿用
`dsh-wsl`。组合包的 patch 用相对路径指向自身入口，因此 `node_modules` 下的文件夹名可以
不同——必须一致的是你安装时使用的那个名字。

1. 将本包加入 DSH 的 profile（`profiles/<profile>/package.json`）：

```json
   { "dependencies": { "dsh-wsl-tool": "file:<path-to-this-repo>" } }
   ```

或运行 `dsh plugin add --profile <profile> dsh-wsl-tool` 从 npm 安装，或用
   `dsh plugin add --profile <profile> file:<path-to-this-repo>` 从本地检出安装
   （依赖名会取本包自身的名字）。

2. 不必再做别的。本包的 `cordis.patch.yml` 会在组合包加载时**自己插入** `tool-wsl` 行
   （进程级），因此这些工具对所有 agent preset 都可用，无需额外接线。**不需要选择任何模式，
   也不要在 preset 里加任何东西**——左侧栏的 WSL 面板同样是这样出现的。

**不要**再在 preset 里列一遍 `tool-wsl`：DSH 按名字注册工具，第二次注册会直接失败
   —— `tool "wsl" is already registered in this scope`。这一行只由组合包提供。

3. 重启 DSH。

设置面板是唯一可选的一块：它的表单需要 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`，多数 profile 已经有了
（只要装过任何依赖它的插件；没有的话把它加进 profile 的依赖即可）。没有它时，工具与
面板里的「WSL 终端启动路径」照常可用，只是开关不显示 —— 面板会直接说明这一点，不会一直转圈等待。

清单里声明了它需要的 DSH —— `"engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.1-rc.2" }`。有两处会依据这条声明
行动：插件市场把它在条目上标成要求，并在装到更老的宿主上之前给出提醒；宿主自己的安装门禁也会
拒绝「声明的范围不含当前 DSH」的版本。**只支持 0.2.1 及更新版本**：旧代终端兼容层（DSH ≤0.2.0，
插件可以通过 `terminalController.follow`/`write` 直接驱动浏览器终端）已经删除，终端工具在这些
宿主上会明确报告「无法驱动终端」，而不是伸手进你的 shell。其余五个工具只是普通的 subprocess
调用，在老宿主上仍然能跑，但包本身不再作出那个支持承诺。

已在 DSH **0.2.1-rc.5** 上验证（更早的 0.2.1-rc.3 同样验证过）：工具 schema 通过 DSH 自己的 `assertSupportedJsonSchema`；
subprocess 接缝是跑在**真实 provider** 上而非替身；后台任务路径跑在**真实 job 注册表**上，
包含「会话 id 属主围栏」（0.2.1 的 job id 是 `kind-<16 hex>`，所以检查读注册表给的那个 id，
而不是假定形状）。这套检查就是 `test/real-seam.mjs`，约一分钟即可重验一个新宿主——升级后把它
指向新的 DSH 安装即可：

```sh
DSH_SUBPROCESS_LOCAL=/path/to/dsh/node_modules npm run test:real
```

后台任务由**调用方会话**持有（`owner: exec.agent.id`），这既是模型能用
`job_output`/`job_kill` 读回它的依据，也是其他会话读不到它的围栏；exec 里没有 agent 时
任务则是无主的。

终端工具有两条受支持的驱动路径：**浏览器桥**（0.2.1：由本插件的浏览器半加入你打开的侧边栏终端，
宿主把 `attach`/`write`/`detach` 经 `/dsh-wsl-tool/term-bridge/poll` 与 `/events` 交给页面，
页面用结果、屏幕快照与输出作答）和**私有 PTY**（工具自己的活用 `subprocess.spawnTerminal`
开一个自己的 shell——动作相同、输入框上方的记录相同，只是这个 shell 工具私有，你打开的终端不受影响）。
两条路径都有 `npm test` 覆盖。

readme.section: 左侧栏的 WSL 面板
readme.text:
| 开关 | 管什么 |
|---|---|
| `wsl` 命令执行 | 是否注册 `wsl` 工具 |
| `wsl-path` 路径转换 | 是否注册 `wsl-path` 工具 |
| `wsl-env` 能力体检 | 是否注册 `wsl-env` 工具 |
| `wsl-doctor` 项目体检 | 是否注册 `wsl-doctor`，**默认关**：诊断类工具按需开启 |
| `wsl-bootstrap` 安装工具链 | 是否注册 `wsl-bootstrap`，它可能往发行版里装东西。**默认关**，且每次调用还得显式关掉 `dryRun` |
| 后台任务 | `wsl` 是否接受 `runInBackground` |
| 自动转换路径 | 每次调用的 `translatePaths` 默认值 |
| 默认跟随会话工作区 | 未传 `workdir` 时从会话目录开始，而不是 `~`。**默认开**：关掉的话，agent 写的相对路径都会落进 Linux 家目录 —— 那儿在资源管理器里看不见，还会撑大 WSL 磁盘镜像 |
| Linux 默认工作目录 | 未传 `workdir` 时使用的固定 Linux 目录（如 `/mnt/d/project`）。填了就优先于上面的开关；清空则先看 `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR`，没设才回到跟随会话 |
| WSL 终端启动路径 | 可选的侧边栏终端从哪个目录启动 —— 写进你 **profile patch** 里 `terminal-controller` 那一行的 `--cd <目录>`（见[可选：在侧边栏开一个 WSL 终端](#可选在侧边栏开一个-wsl-终端)）。留空则删掉该参数；当前值也是从这个文件读的 |
| 终端历史行数 | 那个终端保留多少行输出（同一行上的 `scrollback`）。平台默认 1000；填 `0` 不保留，留空回到默认。这两项都在重启 DSH 后生效 |
| 危险命令守卫 | 危险命令是否必须显式 `allowDangerous` |
| 管理员模式（root） | `wsl` 与四个文件工具是否接受 `asRoot: true`（`wsl -u root`）。WSL 的 root 免密，所以这项开关就是授权本身；**默认关** |

readme.section: 左侧栏的 WSL 面板
readme.text:
面板改的是插件自己的配置，所以同样的值也可以手写进 profile patch（`- id: tool-wsl` 加 `config:`）
或用环境变量设。优先级由 `lib/config.js` 定：**插件配置 > 环境变量 > 内置默认值**；开关停在默认值时
下层说了算。所以从没打开过面板的人设 `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR` 依然生效——即使「跟随会话工作区」还停在默认的
开：环境变量是显式的部署决定，说话比开关的默认值响。

「WSL 终端启动路径」是唯一的例外：侧边栏终端属于另一个插件，所以那个输入框改的是你 profile 的
patch 层 —— 每次写入前先备份该文件，只重写终端那一行的 `args`，写后还会读回来核对，只要不是"只改了
这一行"就当场还原。

**改动在下次启动 DSH 后生效**：宿主每次挂载只读一次该配置，面板里也写着这句。发行版与超时属于"值"
而不是"功能"：在 patch 里或用 `DSH_WSL_DISTRO` / `DSH_WSL_TIMEOUT_MS` 设置，面板只显示当前生效值。

readme.section: 左侧栏的 WSL 面板
readme.text:
这个设置界面需要 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（插件把它声明为可选 peer 依赖）：没有它工具照常按
默认值工作，只是没有面板。

面板**最底部**是一个反馈入口，旁边跟着一段简短的提交指南，以及一个「复制插件信息」按钮（详见
[反馈](#反馈)）。按钮会向宿主半的 `/dsh-wsl-tool/info` 索取本插件自己的信息 —— 包名、版本、仓库
（都从 `package.json` 读出）、Node 与平台 —— 外加**它正运行在哪个 DSH 构建里**、以及 `wsl-env`
那一套 WSL 事实（默认发行版、内核、能力标记），然后连同当前生效的配置一起复制出来。
这些值没有一个是"发版时要记得手改"的字符串；探测失败时它写明失败，绝不编造。

readme.section: 可选：在侧边栏开一个 WSL 终端
readme.text:
桌面版侧边栏终端可以开 WSL 而不是 Windows shell。这是**可选**的 —— 装插件**不会**改你终端默认
开什么 —— 启用用的 patch 随包提供：[`extras/terminal-wsl.patch.yml`](extras/terminal-wsl.patch.yml)。

启用方式：把里面的条目复制进你自己 profile 的 patch 层
（`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`）；命令行启动也可以改成
`--patch <已安装文件路径>`。**下次启动应用时生效。**

readme.section: 可选：在侧边栏开一个 WSL 终端
readme.text:
这个启动目录也能在面板里设：顶部的「WSL 终端启动路径」（挨着「默认 Linux 工作目录」）会从那个
文件读出当前值，再把 `--cd <目录>` 写到该行 `args` 上 —— 写前先备份 patch 文件，只改这一行，
写后读回来核对。**清空**则删掉该参数，终端回到跟随会话工作区（启动时的 Windows 目录会被翻译成
`/mnt/…`）；填 `~` 固定到 Linux 家目录。改完同样**重启 DSH 生效**。

它旁边的「终端历史行数」在**同一行**上设置 `scrollback`：终端保留多少行输出，长构建才不会被滚掉
（平台默认 1000 行）。填 `0` 表示不保留，留空则回到默认。历史越长，应用与宿主两侧占用的内存越多，
所以这是一个由你决定的数字，而不是一个固定的大值。写入规则与生效时机（重启 DSH）都与上面一致。

```yaml
- id: terminal-controller
  config:
    shell:
      path: 'C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe'

readme.section: 可选：在侧边栏开一个 WSL 终端
readme.text:
- 「新建终端」的列表来自组合里的 `terminal-controller` 行：它把配置的 `shell` 排在最前，同时保留
  它发现的 `powershell`/`cmd`/`bash` 等可选。那个选择列表属于核心 UI，所以**按 id 覆盖该行**是
  受支持的入口 —— 这也是它没法做成普通插件条目的原因。
- **不锁定发行版**：`wsl.exe` 跟随系统默认，与工具在未设 `DSH_WSL_DISTRO` 时的规则一致。要锁定就
  在 `args` 里加 `-d <名字>`。
- 会话工作区是 Windows 路径，`wsl.exe` 会自动翻译，因此终端像 Windows shell 一样落在
  `/mnt/<盘>/…`；而且是**真 PTY**（`xterm-256color`），全屏程序可用。
- 按 id 的 patch 会**整段替换**该行 config，你之前在该行上设过的东西（终端上限、scrollback、
  自定义 `shellCandidates`）要一并重述。

readme.section: WSL 终端里的 `dsh` 命令
readme.text:
在 WSL 里可以直接对桌面版说话：

```sh
dsh -- "帮我把 nemu 的编译错误修掉"
```

这句话进入面板指定的 DSH 会话——客户端里看到同一条消息和同一段回复——终端这边
流式显示：先出现思考计时，回答逐字回来，结束时一行汇总（耗时、步数、
token）。按 `Ctrl+C` 只是停止等待，那一轮会在客户端里继续跑完。

终端就是这段对话的另一个入口：输入原样转发过去，客户端把回复流式转回——终端会显示思考计时，
但不显示思考内容。会话正在回答时，这行输入以 steer 方式送入当前回合，不排队、也不会丢。

readme.section: WSL 终端里的 `dsh` 命令
readme.text:
| 命令 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `dsh -- "问题"` | 发给当前会话，流式显示回复（`--` 之后是消息，可以不加引号） |
| `dsh <id> -- "问题"` | 发给指定会话 |
| `dsh list` | 列出会话（最新在前，`*` 表示当前） |
| `dsh new <id>` | 新建会话（客户端里会出现）并切换过去 |
| `dsh use <id>` | 切换当前会话 |
| `dsh rm <id>` | 归档会话（客户端自己的可恢复删除） |
| `dsh status` | 当前会话与通道状态 |

消息必须带 `--` 标记；第一个词会被当成**命令**，所以打错的命令（例如 `dsh statsu`）会直接报「不存在此命令」并提示用法，而不会被当成问题发给模型。用标记而不是"有没有引号"来判断，是因为 shell 在脚本看到参数之前就把引号去掉了——`--` 是唯一还能区分「这是消息」的东西。

readme.section: WSL 终端里的 `dsh` 命令
readme.text: 终端里发来的消息在对话里带 **【WSL 终端】** 前缀，一眼就能和客户端输入区分；⏱ 思考计时会**持续跳动**，按「几分几秒」显示（`0分05秒`、`1分23秒`），不会停在第一个数字上。shim 每个通道实例只解析一次传输路径（以前每条命令都要探测被防火墙静默丢包的那条）；宿主接受请求后立刻显示**… 已送达，等待模型 Ns** 的实时计时，等待可见而不是像卡住。这段等待是模型的，不是通道的：同一台机器实测宿主 2–20 ms 就确认，shim 再加约 0.1 s；而一个回合在小会话上约 1.8 s，在带着约 18.2 万输入 token 的面板落点上要 4.8 s。回合结束后，终端会打印当前登录的 DeepSeek 账户余额（充值余额与赠金，按账户面板的格式）；未登录或暂时读不到会如实说明，不会显示成 `¥0.00`。余额是在模型工作时后台取的，不会拖慢回复。终端聊天嫌慢时，给它单独开一个精简会话（`dsh new terminal` 然后 `dsh use terminal`），别用那个很大的落点会话，或者先压缩它。不碰模型的子命令很便宜：`dsh use` 只改一个本地文件（约 15 ms，不碰通道），`dsh new`/`dsh rm` 一次往返，`dsh list` 直接返回缓存的会话行并后台刷新（通道启动后的第一次会完整重建）。需要联系宿主的命令约有 0.1 s 下限，那是 `curl.exe` 的进程启动时间：本机 WSL 自己的 curl 到 Windows 宿主网卡被丢包，所以 shim 有意使用 Windows 客户端。

readme.section: WSL 终端里的 `dsh` 命令
readme.text:
发自终端的 `dsh -- "…"` 如果目标正是「正在执行这条命令的会话」，会被直接拒绝并说明原因：消息会加入那一轮，而那一轮要等命令返回——会自锁。这种场景等这一轮结束，或者在客户端里输入。只有插件的终端工具启动的 shell 才会带上调用方会话（`x-dsh-wsl-caller`），你自己在终端里输入不受影响。

回复流式输出期间终端没有提示符，但它仍然可以输入：**先按一次回车暂停输出**，敲完内容再回车就作为插入（steer）发进同一段对话，随后继续输出并显示 `已插入当前对话，继续输出`；第二次回车留空则取消插入。设 `DSH_WSL_NO_STEER=1` 可关掉这个输入；管道/脚本不会启用它，只有真终端才会。

readme.section: WSL 终端里的 `dsh` 命令
readme.text: 终端发来的消息就**只是你敲的那句话**——屏幕内容不会出现在对话里。但你看到的画面仍然会到模型那里：宿主按命令行本身找到那条命令所在的侧边栏终端，只读地抓最近 100 行屏幕，作为**下一次模型请求的隐藏运行时上下文**（和「工作目录」、记忆插件用的是同一个 `systemPrompt` context 机制；只用一次、不写进对话）。还不够的话，模型可以用本插件自己的终端工具（`wsl-term read`，只读）再读同一个终端。识别是尽力而为且有上限的——没有打开的 DSH 窗口、找不到匹配终端、或读得太慢，就干脆不带，而且最多让回合晚开始约 3 秒。工具调用里发起的 prompt 不带上下文：那句话不是有人在终端里敲的。

readme.section: WSL 终端里的 `dsh` 命令
readme.text:
在面板里设置一次：打开 **启用 dsh 命令**、点 **安装 dsh 命令**。默认落点是**最近活跃的会话**（通常就是你正在看的那段对话）；想换落点，在下拉里选中另一段会话（或当场新建）即可（脚本装到
`~/.local/bin/dsh`）。之后插件会自己维护它：每次启动（以及改设置）时读一次已安装的脚本，发现缺失或比当前版本旧就自动重装，不用再点按钮——这次检查只花一次 `cat`，通道关闭时和有回合在流式输出时都不碰 WSL；想关掉自动安装，把插件配置里的 `autoInstallShim` 设为 `false`。通道是插件绑在 WSL 默认网关地址上的一个小 HTTP 服务，随机端口，
每个请求都要带本次启动生成的令牌。桌面版需要在运行；指定的会话就是普通会话——通道
发进去的是一条普通用户消息（带「【WSL 终端】」前缀），所以客户端里看到的是同一段回复。

| 参数 | 必填 | 类型 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | 是 | string | 要执行的 Linux 命令 |
| `description` | 是 | string | 简短的界面说明文字 |
| `workdir` | 否 | string | Linux 路径（`/home/me`、`~/src`）或 Windows 路径，默认 `~` |
| `timeoutMs` | 否 | number | 超时毫秒数，默认 600000（10 分钟）；到点后杀进程并把结果标记为超时 |
| `distro` | 否 | string | WSL 发行版；默认使用系统默认发行版 |
| `env` | 否 | object | 要导出的额外环境变量（键必须是合法 shell 变量名） |
| `stdin` | 否 | string | 在命令运行前写入其 stdin 的文本（UTF-8） |
| `runInBackground` | 否 | boolean | 作为后台任务运行并立即返回任务 id；用 `job_output` 读、`job_kill` 停 |
| `allowDangerous` | 否 | boolean | 置 `true` 才允许执行危险命令 |
| `asRoot` | 否 | boolean | 本次调用以 root 执行（`wsl -u root`）；面板「管理员模式」关着时会被拒绝 |
| `translatePaths` | 否 | boolean | 默认 `true`；置 `false` 时 `command` 原样传入，不做路径改写 |

面板里的开关与取值字段（`tools.wsl`、`tools.path`、`tools.env`、`tools.doctor`、
`tools.bootstrap`、`tools.read`、`tools.write`、`tools.edit`、`tools.grep`、`backgroundJobs`、
`translatePaths`、`startInSessionWorkspace`、`workdir`、`dangerGuard`、`allowRoot`、
`distro`、`timeoutMs`）都写在 profile patch 里，各自行上有说明。
其中两项**故意没有环境变量**：`dangerGuard`（它的关闭位置本身就是风险）与 `allowRoot`
（WSL 的 root 免密，所以那项开关就是授权本身）。环境变量这一层：

| 环境变量 | 默认值 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_WSL_DISTRO` | （系统默认） | 为所有调用固定发行版 |
| `DSH_WSL_TIMEOUT_MS` | `600000` | 模型命令的默认超时；单次调用可用 `timeoutMs` 覆盖 |
| `DSH_WSL_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` | `86400000` | 单次 `timeoutMs` 的上限，对齐平台 shell 工具的 `maxTimeoutMs`；默认超时也受它约束 |
| `DSH_WSL_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` | `65536` | 每条流的内存窗口（1 KiB – 8 MiB）；设到 64 MiB 以上时也会抬高落盘上限 |
| `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR` | （未设：交给开关） | 不传 `workdir` 时的起点：`home`（Linux 的 `~`）、`session`（会话工作目录，Windows 检出对应 `/mnt/<盘>/...`），或任意显式路径（Windows 路径同样会被转换）。显式设置时优先于「跟随会话工作区」的默认开；不设时由开关决定 |

无法解析或越界的值会回退到默认值——一个写错的环境变量不该让所有工具一起挂掉。
**改动即时生效**（包括工具开关）：注册工具时会拿到它自己的 disposer，所以每次设置更新都会把期望的工具集
与已注册的工具集做差分，开关一拨工具就出现或消失，不需要重启——这一点重要，因为开关就是在面板里拨的。
唯一例外是「WSL 终端启动路径」：它改的是别的插件在 profile patch 里的启动参数，那个插件在启动时读，
所以那一项要重启 DSH。

- 每次调用都在全新的 shell 中执行——cwd / 变量 / 函数不会在调用间保留。
- **stdin 默认是 `/dev/null`，除非传 `stdin`**：交互式命令（`read`、`cat`、不带 `-S`
  的 `sudo` 密码提示）否则会立刻收到 EOF，无法等待输入；本插件不会、也无法弹出任何提示。
  通过 `stdin` 传的密码会被记进会话记录。
- 什么都不配时从会话工作目录开始（「跟随会话工作区」默认开）；要落到 `~` 就设
  `DSH_WSL_WORKDIR=home`，也可显式写 `session` 或固定路径（见“配置”）。
- 发行版取调用参数 → `DSH_WSL_DISTRO` → 系统默认，代码里不再硬编码兜底名称。
- 发行版不存在时会给出明确报错（`distribution "X" is not registered`），而不是
  一个原始 `-1` 退出码；其他启动器错误（`Wsl/Service/WSL_E_*`）也会带错误码上报，
  不会被当成命令自身的退出状态。
- **后台任务可以活得比这次调用久**：`runInBackground: true` 立即返回任务 id（`wsl-N`）
  并把工作登记进宿主任务注册表，`job_output` 读它（标记与前台一致）、`job_kill` 停它。
  后台模式下 10 分钟默认超时**不适用**，但显式 `timeoutMs` 仍然生效；非零退出与前台一样
  报成 `completed` 并把退出码写进 detail。
- `command`、`workdir` 以及配置/`DSH_WSL_WORKDIR` 给出的默认目录中的 Windows 路径会自动转换为 `/mnt/...`：
  - `C:\Users\me\a.txt` → `/mnt/c/Users/me/a.txt`；含空格、括号的路径与一行多个路径都支持
    （`C:\Program Files\Git`、`C:/Program Files/Git`、`C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam`、
    `cp C:\a.txt D:\b.txt` 两个路径都会转换）；
  - `\\wsl.localhost\<发行版>\home\x` 与 `\\wsl$\<发行版>\home\x` → `/home/x`；指向**别的发行版**的
    UNC 路径保持原样（否则 `/home/x` 会变成当前发行版的目录，读错东西）；
  - 只是"看起来像"盘符的文本不会被动：单个小写字母后跟 `/`（如 `a:/b`）、其他表达式里的
    盘符（如 `sed "s/C:\x/y/"`）、URL 里的疑似盘符段；
  - 当路径要交给**Wind

```
  [stdout truncated: at most the last 65536 of 1288895 bytes were kept; full stream: C:\...\stdout.log]
  ```
- `timeoutMs` 默认 10 分钟，避免卡死的 `wsl.exe` 永久挂住调用；需要长时间运行的命令可以传更大的值，
  但上限是 `DSH_WSL_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`（默认 24 小时）——手滑不会变成"永不超时"。结果里回报的始终是
  **实际生效**的那个期限。到点会连 Linux 侧进程一起杀掉（Windows 上由 provider 使用 `taskkill /T /F`）。
- **宿主 shell 的环境事实会转发进发行版**（WSL 默认不跨边界传 Windows 环境变量）：`DSH_SESSION_ID`、
  `DSH_SHELL`、以及翻译成 `/mnt/...` 形式的 `DSH_HOME` 会在命令前 `export`，脚本因此能看到与平台自带
  shell 工具一致的会话事实。这些值**按次**从宿主的 `shellEnv` 注册表解析（与其他 shell 工具同一个来源），
  因为它们属于会话而非宿主常量——直接读宿主 `process.env` 会什么都读不到、静默地什么都不转发。
  **`DSH_WEB_URL` 故意不转发**——它是 Windows 侧服务的 `127.0.0.1` 地址，
  而默认 NAT 模式下 WSL 访问不到 Windows 回环（实测 `127.0.0.1` 与主机 IP 均返回 HTTP 000，服务本身
  也只绑回环），转进去只会给一个打不开的 URL。显式传入的 `env` 条目总是覆盖转发值。
- `wsl-env` 还会报出**会话文件所在的位置**以及它是否落在 Windows 盘挂载上：

```
  workspace: /mnt/d/DSHworkarea (Windows drive mount /mnt/d — builds, installs and git are much slower here; prefer a path under /home when it matters)
  ```

这个提示值得当真。作者机器实测：128 MB 顺序写在 ext4 上约 **2.1 GB/s**，在 `/mnt/d` 上约
  **247 MB/s**；创建 400 个小文件 ext4 **不到 10 ms**，`/mnt/d` 要 **0.72 s**
  （后来复测：**885 vs 116 MB/s**、**13 ms vs 745 ms**，比值稳定在约 8× 与 50×）。

不只是慢。`/mnt/<盘>` 是 9p（drvfs）挂载，保留的是 **Windows** 的文件系统语义：
  `chmod`/`chown` 不生效（`chmod 600` 读回来是 `777`）、文件名**大小写不敏感**（大小写写错只在
  Linux CI 上才炸）、符号链接与可执行位是合成的，而且 **inotify 完全不工作**——发行版里的 watcher
  对两侧写入都收不到任何事件（用 inotify 探针实测：`/mnt/d` 上 Windows 侧写入与 Linux 侧写入均为
  **0 事件**，而同一探针在 ext4 上正常报出创建/修改/关闭写入）。因此 dev server、`--watch` 模式
  与文件监听的测试在 Windows 盘上都是瞎的。需要时把项目放到 `/home` 下：语义、监听事件与上面那档
  速度一次性都回来。
- 危险命令默认被拒绝，除非调用时传 `allowDangerous: true`：
  - **任何递归删除**——`rm -r`、`rm -rf`、`rm -r -f`、`rm -R --force`、`rm --recursive`——
    因为 stdin 指向 `/dev/null` 时不会产生任何提示，`rm -r tree` 会静默删除整棵树。
    每次 `rm` 调用按其所在命令段单独判定，所以 `rm a -f; rm b -r` 不能靠拼接标志蒙过去；
    而作为**参数**出现的 `rm` 只是提及、不是调用，所以 `npm rm -r foo`、`ls rm -r` 照常放行；
  - 往块设备 `dd`、`mkfs`/`mke2fs`、分区/擦除类工具（`fdisk`、`parted`、`wipefs`、`mkswap` …）、
    对准设备的 `truncate`、`find … -delete`、会真删文件的 `git clean`、
    电源控制（`shutdown`、`reboot`、`systemctl reboot` …）、重定向到块设备（SATA/NVMe/virtio、
    `md`、`dm-*`、LVM 的 `mapper`）、fork 炸弹；
  - 防护会读包装器自己的选项**取值**和 shell 的 `-c` 脚本，所以
    `sudo -u root mkfs.ext4 …`、`nice -n 19 reboot`、`timeout 5 reboot`、
    `xargs -I{} poweroff`、`sh -c "reboot"` 都按它们真正执行的命令判定；
    设备/电源类工具只在**命令位置**匹配，因此查看它们是允许的：`man fdisk`、
    `grep -rn reboo

DSH 的文件沙箱在**两个点**实施：shell 执行器（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-sandbox`、`-pwsh-sandbox`，把
argv 包一层过 `ctx.sandbox`）和文件系统服务（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-sandbox`，对两个写操作加策略栅栏）。
**`wsl` 两者都不经过**——它通过宿主 `subprocess` 服务直接拉起 `wsl.exe`，位于那一层之下。因此
`workspace-write` 策略**约束不到它**：它能写 Linux 侧能写的任何位置，也能写 `/mnt/<盘>` 下 Windows
允许的任何位置。

这不是靠"接入沙箱"能补上的缺口。Windows 上的沙箱最终落到 **ACL / 受限令牌**，而文件操作发生在
**Linux 内核里**：写 `/home/...` 动的是发行版自己的文件系统镜像，任何 Windows 令牌都够不着；写
`/mnt/c/...` 要经文件系统桥，ACL 是否生效不可依赖。把 `wsl.exe` 包起来只能约束"启动器"，约束不了写入
——而给出**虚假的隔离感，比明说不隔离更危险**。（平台自己的 `dsh-fs-sandbox` 也坦白它的边界：
"containment, not a security boundary"。）

`wsl` 实际拥有的保护是上面那套危险命令守卫：一份确定性的拒绝清单，**不是内核边界**。请把它当作
"能碰到你的 WSL 安装能碰的一切"来授予权限。

本包声明了 `dsh.bundle` manifest（见 `package.json`），因此仓库被列表收录后可按
名称安装，例如 `dsh plugin add dsh-wsl-tool`，市场（storefront）也会提供一键安装。
上文 `file:` 的本地安装方式仍然有效。

| 模块 | 职责 |
|---|---|
| `lib/config.js` | 默认值与环境变量覆盖，挂载时解析一次 |
| `lib/paths.js` | shell 引号处理与 Windows → WSL 路径转换 |
| `lib/guard.js` | 危险命令规则 |
| `lib/result.js` | 启动器噪声过滤、截断事实、标记渲染 |
| `lib/diagnostics.js` | `wsl-env` 的能力探针、解析器与输出行 |
| `lib/runner.js` | 唯一的 spawn 路径与启动器错误分类 |
| `lib/tools/*.js` | 工具定义（schema / execute / presentCall） |
| `lib/doctor.js` | `wsl-doctor` 的项目探针：一段 shell、它的解析器与报告组装 |
| `lib/bootstrap.js` | `wsl-bootstrap` 的配方、计划生成与结果渲染 |
| `lib/terminal.js` | `wsl-term` 背后的文本与选择逻辑：去转义、命令标记、终端选择 |

- `apply()` 解析配置并注册被启用的工具，每个都有 JSON-schema 参数定义、输出 schema、
  `render` 钩子与异步 `execute`。
- 所有调用都走同一条 spawn 路径（`runner.runWsl`）：通过宿主 `subprocess` 执行
  `wsl.exe -d <distro> -e bash -lc "<exports; cd workdir && command>"`，stdout/stderr
  上限由配置决定（超出最多落盘 64 MiB），abort 后有 3 秒宽限期，超时默认 10 分钟。
  插件自身的探测调用另有 30 秒硬上限，避免 WSL 服务卡死时永久挂住工具调用。
- `env` 条目在命令前部以 `export` 形式注入，确保可靠到达 Linux 侧；Windows 盘符
  路径在构造命令前先改写为 `/mnt/...`。
- 输出为 `{ exitCode, signal, timedOut, timeoutMs, truncated, stdout, stderr,
  stdoutTotalBytes, stdoutDroppedBytes, stderrTotalBytes, stderrDroppedBytes,
  stdoutSpillPath, stderrSpillPath, jobId }`；`render` 钩子将其格式化为文本并附加上述
  标记。截断标记引用窗口大小本身而不是由解码文本推算的数字——窗口起点落在多字节字符
  中间时后者会差一两个字节。
- `jobId` 只有后台启动才会赋值，其余路径一律 `null`，因此两种情况下声明形状都成立。
- 启动与结算被拆成两步（`runner.launch` / `settle`）：后台任务要同步交给注册表一对
  `cancel`/`done`，而前台调用只是 await 同一个 settle。被取消的任务会把 provider 的
  "target 启动前即被终止"拒绝映射成 `killed`——`JobHooks.done` 不允许 reject。
- 危险命令防护把命令按 `;`／`&`／`|`／换行切成段，每次 `rm` 调用按自身标志单独判定，
  设备/电源类工具在命令位置匹配后才拦截。

插件不发布任何自身服务，且由它自己的组合包 patch **进程级**插入，因此既不需要 realm，
也不需要任何 preset 条目。

插件是纯 ESM，无构建步骤，除 DSH 宿主平面外无运行时依赖。迭代方式：把 profile
依赖指向本仓库：

```json
{ "dependencies": { "dsh-wsl-tool": "file:/path/to/dsh-wsl" } }
```

然后重启 DSH，在**任意**会话里调用工具即可：组合包 patch 是进程级注册的，没有哪个 preset
需要声明这一行。

```sh
npm test          # 1579 项宿主检查（跑在真实 WSL 上，仅用 shim 顶替 ctx.subprocess）+ 305 项客户端检查
npm run test:real # 同一套检查改跑真实 provider，外加 seam 事实套件
```

`npm test` 只替换 `ctx.subprocess`，用一个复刻了 seam 行为（有界尾窗、落盘文件、
终止阶梯）的 shim 驱动这些工具跑在真实 WSL 上，覆盖路径改写、workdir 引号处理、
危险命令防护、发行版选择、退出码/超时/截断标记、`wsl-path`、`wsl-env`、参数校验、
配置解析、启动器错误分类、返回结构与各自 `output.schema` 的一致性，以及模型可见
目录的 token 预算。

`npm run test:real` 把同一套检查改跑在 `LocalSubprocessRuntime` 上——shim 不允许与
真实 seam 漂移——然后跑 `test/real-seam.mjs`，校验 shim 无法担保的事实
（`readFrom(0).nextOffset` 是否为整条流字节总数、落盘文件是否完整、超时是否真的杀掉
`wsl.exe` 的 Linux 侧进程），并用 DSH 自己的 `assertSupportedJsonSchema` 校验全部
schema。它需要一份 DSH 安装：

```sh
DSH_SUBPROCESS_LOCAL=/path/to/dsh/node_modules npm run test:real
```

`file:` 依赖是**副本**，改本仓库不会改变 DSH 实际加载的内容。任何改动之后：

```sh
npm run sync                  # 复制到 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-wsl
npm run sync -- /path/to/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/<你的依赖名>
```

目标目录必须是 profile 依赖名对应的文件夹（上面的默认值就是本检出的依赖名）；
插件按相对路径加载自身入口，因此文件夹叫什么并不影响加载。

然后重启 DSH——插件在加载时只导入一次。
